prerequisites: Identify idgham with ghunnah in ي ن م و.
Identify idgham without ghunnah in ل ر.
Distinguish the target sound from its ghunnah characteristic.
learningOutcomes: Classify ن م ل ر as complete idgham.
Classify ي و as incomplete idgham.
Explain that the ghunnah characteristic remains with ي and و.
Classify and recite representative examples accurately.

linguistic.ar: الكامل هو التام، والناقص هو ما بقي منه أثر.
linguistic.en: Complete means fully accomplished; incomplete means that a characteristic remains.

technical.ar: الإدغام الكامل تذهب فيه ذات النون الساكنة أو التنوين وصفتها، ويكون مع ن م ل ر. والإدغام الناقص تذهب فيه ذات النون وتبقى صفة الغنة، ويكون مع ي و.
technical.en: In complete idgham, the noon or tanween is fully absorbed; this classification includes ن، م، ل، and ر. In incomplete idgham, the noon itself is absorbed while its ghunnah characteristic remains; this occurs with ي and و.

studentFriendly.ar: مع ن م ل ر يكتمل الإدغام. ومع ي و تختفي النون لكن تبقى غنتها، لذلك يسمى الإدغام ناقصًا.
studentFriendly.en: With ن م ل ر the merging is complete. With ي و the noon disappears but its ghunnah remains, so the merging is called incomplete.

definition.memoryFormula: كامل: ن م ل ر  |  ناقص: ي و

keyTerms.en: the ghunnah characteristic that remains with ي and و

teacherPreparation: Prepare two columns: complete ن م ل ر and incomplete ي و.
Reuse examples the learner already knows so the new challenge is classification.
Avoid turning terminology into a substitute for correct recitation.
Use color to show what disappears and what remains.

openingReview.teacherPrompt: Ask for the six idgham letters.
Sort them into with-ghunnah and without-ghunnah groups.
Ask what remains during idgham with ya and waw.

conceptExplanation.text: Complete versus incomplete does not mean correct versus incorrect. Both are correct types. The names describe whether the ghunnah characteristic of noon remains after merging.
Keep two classifications separate: with/without ghunnah describes performance; complete/incomplete describes the extent of absorption.

lessonPath.title: Separate
lessonPath.text: Distinguish the letter identity from its ghunnah.

lessonPath.title: Classify
lessonPath.text: Complete: ن م ل ر; incomplete: ي و.

lessonPath.title: Compare
lessonPath.text: Use familiar examples side by side.

lessonPath.title: Apply
lessonPath.text: Name both idgham classifications before reciting.

visualExplanation.display: ن م ل ر ← إدغام كامل  |  ي و ← إدغام ناقص لبقاء الغنة
visualExplanation.teacherUse: Ask what remains with each group.

ruleSummary.condition: A valid two-word idgham boundary has one of the six idgham letters.
ruleSummary.result: Classify ن م ل ر as complete and ي و as incomplete.
ruleSummary.location: Across two words, after noon saakinah or tanween.

quranExamples.arabic: وَمَا بِكُم مِّن نِّعْمَةٍ فَمِنَ ٱللَّهِ
quranExamples.readingInstruction: Merge fully into the strengthened noon with its required ghunnah.
quranExamples.teacherExplanation: Noon belongs to the complete-idgham group.

quranExamples.readingInstruction: Merge fully into mim while maintaining the ghunnah of the strengthened mim.
quranExamples.teacherExplanation: Mim is complete idgham even though ghunnah is present.
quranExamples.commonError: Classifying mim with ya and waw merely because all use ghunnah.

quranExamples.readingInstruction: Merge fully into lam without retaining the idgham ghunnah.
quranExamples.commonError: Assuming complete idgham must always have ghunnah.

quranExamples.readingInstruction: Merge fully into ra without a two-count idgham ghunnah.
quranExamples.commonError: Adding ra to the incomplete group.

quranExamples.arabic: فَمَن يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْرًا يَرَهُۥ
quranExamples.readingInstruction: Merge the noon identity into ya while retaining a two-count ghunnah.
quranExamples.teacherExplanation: Ya is incomplete because the ghunnah characteristic remains.

quranExamples.readingInstruction: Merge into waw while retaining the two-count ghunnah.
quranExamples.commonError: Classifying waw as complete because the noon is not heard separately.

guidedPractice.feedback: Do not allow the two classification systems to be mixed.

guidedPractice.studentAction: Classify, explain what remains, then recite.
guidedPractice.feedback: Terminology must be followed by correct performance.

interactiveActivities.feedbackCorrect: Correct. Complete idgham includes noon, mim, lam, and ra.
interactiveActivities.feedbackIncorrect: The complete group combines ن م with ل ر.

interactiveActivities.feedbackCorrect: Correct. Ya and waw retain the ghunnah characteristic.
interactiveActivities.feedbackIncorrect: The incomplete pair is ي و.

instruction.en: Why is idgham with ya incomplete?

interactiveActivities.feedbackCorrect: Correct. The noon identity is absorbed but its ghunnah remains.
interactiveActivities.feedbackIncorrect: Focus on what remains after merging.

instruction.en: Does complete idgham always mean without ghunnah?

interactiveActivities.feedbackCorrect: Correct. Noon and mim are complete idgham with ghunnah.
interactiveActivities.feedbackIncorrect: Complete/incomplete and with/without ghunnah are different classifications.

interactiveActivities.feedbackCorrect: Correct. Noon belongs to the complete group.
interactiveActivities.feedbackIncorrect: Do not classify by the presence of ghunnah alone.

interactiveActivities.feedbackCorrect: Correct. Mim is complete idgham with ghunnah.
interactiveActivities.feedbackIncorrect: Mim belongs with ن م ل ر.

interactiveActivities.feedbackCorrect: Correct. Ra is complete idgham without ghunnah.
interactiveActivities.feedbackIncorrect: Ra belongs with ن م ل ر.

interactiveActivities.feedbackCorrect: Correct. The ghunnah remains with ya.
interactiveActivities.feedbackIncorrect: Ya belongs to the incomplete pair.

interactiveActivities.feedbackCorrect: Correct. Waw belongs to the incomplete pair.
interactiveActivities.feedbackIncorrect: The ghunnah characteristic remains with waw.

instruction.en: A learner says mim is incomplete because it has ghunnah. What is the correction?

items: Mim is complete idgham with ghunnah
acceptedAnswers: Mim is complete idgham with ghunnah
interactiveActivities.feedbackCorrect: Correct. Keep the two classification systems separate.
interactiveActivities.feedbackIncorrect: Presence of ghunnah alone does not decide complete versus incomplete.

instruction.en: A learner removes ghunnah before waw. What is missing?

interactiveActivities.feedbackCorrect: Correct. Its presence is why the idgham is incomplete.

interactiveActivities.feedbackIncorrect: The incomplete pair is ya and waw.

interactiveActivities.prompt: Why is فَمَن يَعْمَلْ incomplete idgham?
items: Noon merges into ya but its ghunnah remains
acceptedAnswers: Noon merges into ya but its ghunnah remains
interactiveActivities.feedbackCorrect: Excellent. You explained both absorption and the remaining characteristic.
interactiveActivities.feedbackIncorrect: State what disappears and what remains.

commonMistakes: Classifying mim as incomplete because ghunnah is present.
Forgetting that ya and waw form the incomplete pair.
Using terminology correctly while reciting incorrectly.
correctionTechniques: Use a two-axis table: ghunnah performance and extent of absorption.
Ask two questions separately: Is there ghunnah? Is the idgham complete?
Reuse the same six examples until classification is automatic.
Require a spoken reason before recitation.

knowledgeChecks.success: ن م ل ر and ي و are correct.

teacherQuestions: Is the idgham complete or incomplete?
studentTasks: Explain why mim is complete despite ghunnah.
independentPractice: Create a table for all six idgham letters.
For each letter, write with/without ghunnah and complete/incomplete.
homework: Classify six teacher-approved examples using both systems.
Recite one complete-with-ghunnah and one incomplete example.
exitTicket: Name the complete and incomplete groups.
masteryCriteria: Keeps the two classification systems separate.
Explains what remains in incomplete idgham.
teacherNotes: This is primarily a conceptual organization lesson using already learned recitation.
Do not imply that incomplete means defective.
Teacher listening remains the final test of performance.
